Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY DILG OPINION NO. 19 S. 09 March 2010 MISS JAYNE B. RIZAL SK Federation President City of Calamba, Laguna Dear Miss Rizal: 20J O This pertains to your request for legal opinion on whether or not the Sangguniang Panlungsod can allocate funds for the allowance of Sangguniang Kabataan Kagawads. Per your letter, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Calamba is providing allowances for Barangay Nutrition Scholars, Barangay Health Workers, Barangay Tanods, Lupong Tagapamayapa and other appointed officials. Thus, you believe that the seven members of the Sangguniang Kabataan (commonly known as SK Kagawads), as elective officials, are also entitled to receive allowances. Before dwelling on your query, may we invite your attention to our DILG Opinion No. 11, series of 2009 dated 23 February 2009, wherein we clarified that SK Officials are considered elective barangay officials. This is based on the pronouncement made by the Supreme Court in Marquez vs. COMELEC (G.R. No. 127318, 25 August 1999) and is consistent with Article 71, Rule XIV of the Rules and Regulations• Implementing RA 7160 which includes members of the SK in the enumeration of elective barangay officials. Article 71, Rule XIV of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 provides. "Article 71. ELECTIVE LOCAL OFFICIALS. - The elective officials of provinces, cities, municipalities and barangay are the following: xxx (For the Barangays) (a) Punong Barangay; xxx xxx (b) Members of the Sangguniang Barangay; and (c) Members of the Sangguniang Kabataan." Section 423 of the Local Government Code of 1991 also provides the composition of the Barangay Sangguniang Kabataan and we quote:

2- "SECTION 423. CREATION AND ELECTION - (a) There shall be in every barangay a Sangguniang Kabataan to be composed of a chairman, seven (7) members, a secretary and a treasured'. Based on the above-cited provisions, it is clear that the seven members SK Kagawads are considered elective barangay officials. At this juncture, it may be well to know that Section 393 of the Local Government Code provides the benefits of the barangay officials and we quote: "SECTION 393. , BENEFITS OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS. - (a) Barangay Officials, including barangay tanods and members of the lupong tagapamayapa, shall receive honoraria, allowances, and such other emoluments as may be authorized by law or barangay, municipal or city ordinance in accordance with the provisions of this Code, xxx xxx xxx Provided, however, that the annual appropriations for personal services shall be subject to the budgetary limitations prescribed under Title Five, Book II of this Code". (Underlining ours) As already discussed above, SK kagawads are considered barangay officials. Such being the case and applying therefore the aforequoted Section 393 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991, said SK kagawads may receive such allowance, provided however that the same must be duly authorized by law or barangay, municipal or city ordinance. Be that as it may, if the City of Calamba through the issuance of an ordinance grants the SK Kagawad such allowance, please note however, that it is not demandable as a matter of right but it is still subject to the discretion of the City of Calamba granting the same. Provided further, that if the City of Calamba grants the said allowance to the SK Kagawads, the annual appropriations ordinance which allocated funds for that purpose complies with the budgetary requirements and limitations set forth in Sections 324 and 325 of the Code (Local Government Code). Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY. ATTY. JE ir tor Ill DIR. JOSEFINA E. CASTILLA-GO Regional Director DILG-Region IV-A cegaIi94 /rb#23
